rules.title: Every prediction states an uncertainty interval
rules.description: The output carries an interval with lower and upper bounds and a stated level.
rules.rationale: A bare point estimate implies a precision it does not have. The interval is what tells a reader whether 0.62 means somewhere between a coin flip and a near certainty, or something genuinely narrow.
rules.remediation: Add the interval, its level, and ideally the method used to derive it.

rules.title: The interval is coherent and contains the estimate
rules.description: The lower bound does not exceed the upper bound, the point estimate lies within them, and the level is strictly between 0 and 1.
rules.rationale: An interval that excludes its own point estimate is a transcription error or a units error, and either way the two numbers were not produced by the same computation.
rules.remediation: Recompute the interval from the same distribution as the point estimate.
